stimuli.description: Two experimental rooms of different sizes (large and small) with 8 chairs arranged in an oval. Large room: 3.02m x 4.11m. Small room: 1.70m x 2.46m.

Interaction means for perceived starkness of room for males and females in small and large rooms.

limitations: The dissimilarities between our experimental situation and the urban environment limit the generality of our findings to macro crowding phenomena.
Subjects experienced crowding for a relatively short period of time and realized that they would eventually leave the situation.

The experiment did not control for or manipulate the factor of time, making it impossible to ascertain whether the perception of crowding actually decreased over time within the small room, competitive condition.

It was impossible to ascertain whether the increased level of laughter and noise perceived in the small room, competitive condition reflected the absence of crowding, a mode of coping with it, or even a nonspatial source of heightened crowding.
